    subgraph "Automation Clients"
        Tests("Tests (Automation Clients)"):::client
        Samples("Samples (Automation Clients)"):::client
        UIRecorder("UI Recorder Tool"):::client
    end

    %% Core Service
    Service("WinAppDriver Service\n(listens on 127.0.0.1:4723)"):::service

    %% Application Under Tests
    AUT("Application Under Tests\n(UWP, WinForms, WPF, Win32)"):::aut

    %% Documentation & Support
    Doc("Documentation & Support"):::doc

    %% Client -> Service interactions
    Tests -->|"sendsRESTcalls"| Service
    Samples -->|"sendsRESTcalls"| Service
    UIRecorder -->|"sendsRESTcalls"| Service

    %% Service -> AUT interaction
    Service -->|"executesUIAutomation"| AUT

    %% AUT -> Service response
    AUT -->|"returnsResponse"| Service

    %% Service -> Clients response
    Service -->|"returnsResponse"| Tests
    Service -->|"returnsResponse"| Samples

<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, this repository is the Windows Application Driver (WinAppDriver) project—a test automation service that supports Selenium-like UI testing on Windows applications (UWP, WinForms, WPF, and Win32). It contains not only the core driver that listens on a configurable IP and port (default 127.0.0.1:4723) but also a wealth of supporting testing samples, test suites, and even a standalone tool (UI Recorder) to automate script generation.

Below is a step-by-step guide on how to create a detailed system design diagram tailored to this project:

1. Identify the Main Components:
   • WinAppDriver Service: The central executable (WinAppDriver.exe) that listens for automation commands. This is the heart of the system and should be highlighted as the driver component.
   • Test Automation Clients: There are comprehensive test suites (under the “Tests” folder) and samples (in the “Samples” directory with subfolders for C#, Java, JavaScript, Python, Ruby) that interact with the WinAppDriver. These represent the client applications invoking the service.
   • Application Under Tests (AUT): The “ApplicationUnderTests” folder holds sample applications built in UWP. These illustrate how the driver is used to automate real Windows apps.
   • UI Recorder Tool: Found under “Tools/UIRecorder”, this standalone tool assists users by recording UI events and generating XPath queries and C# code, thus acting as an integrated recording and code-generation utility.
   • Documentation & Support: The “Docs” folder (along with README, SECURITY, and SUPPORT files) provides guidelines, FAQs, and CI/CD integration instructions which support both user and developer environments.

2. Analyze Relationships and Interactions:
   • Data Flow & Dependency: 
     – Test scripts and automation frameworks (both in Samples and Tests) send UI commands (using WebDriver-like APIs) to the WinAppDriver service.
     – WinAppDriver processes the commands and interacts with the appropriate Windows application (AUT) by executing UI automation commands.
     – The UI Recorder tool can capture user interactions and generate automation scripts that eventually use the same REST endpoints provided by WinAppDriver. 
   • Communication Patterns:
     – The service listens on a specific port/IP address and receives REST-style automation commands (like clicking elements, reading text, etc.) from external clients.
     – The test projects show layered interactions where higher-level tests wrap around lower-level API calls (initializing sessions, element actions, etc.).
   
3. Architectural and Design Patterns:
   • Client-Server Architecture: The separation between test clients (or UI Recorder) and WinAppDriver service exemplifies a clear client-server model.
   • Modular Components: The repository is divided into clear modules – tests, samples, UI recorder, and core service components – emphasizing separation of concerns.
   • API Abstraction: A consistent WebDriver-inspired API is used, enabling support across various Windows application frameworks.
   • Configuration Driven: Multiple project files (e.g., .csproj, project.json, custom.props) stress that configuration and build automation are key parts of the architecture.

4. Diagram Guidelines:
   • Create distinct blocks for each main component:
       - Label one block "WinAppDriver Service" (highlight that it runs as an administrator and listens on a configurable port).
       - Place blocks for “Tests” and “Samples” that use the service. You might want to further subdivide these into language-specific clients if desired.
       - Use another block for “Application Under Tests” to depict the target Windows UWP or desktop applications.
       - Include a block for “UI Recorder” as a tool that interacts both with the WinAppDriver and the code-generation endpoint.
       - Finally, include a block for “Documentation / Support” to reference additional info and best-practices.
   • Use directional arrows to illustrate:
       - How test scripts and UI Recorder send automation commands (an arrow pointing from “Tests/Samples/UI Recorder” to “WinAppDriver Service”).
       - An arrow from the WinAppDriver Service to the “Application Under Tests,” showing that the service drives UI interactions.
       - Feedback: arrows coming back from the AUT to the driver and then to the clients (to show responses, state updates, and error handling).
   • Apply color coding or different shapes:
       - Use one color or shape for automation clients (Tests, Samples, UI Recorder),
       - Another for service components (WinAppDriver core),
       - And a different style for target applications (AUT) and supporting/documentation components.
       
5. Additional Tips for the Diagram:
   • Clearly label each component with their directory name and/or functionality. For example, include notations like “Tests/WebDriverAPI – handles low-level interactions” or “Tools/UIRecorder – records UI tasks.”
   • Reflect any dependency relationships such as configuration files (custom.props, solution files) and how they tie components together.
   • If space allows, include annotations noting key interactions (e.g., “sends REST calls”, “processes XPath queries”, “generates C# code”) to capture the essence of the communication.
   • Ensure that the overall architecture emphasizes a modular design that clearly separates core automation (driver service), clients (tests/samples), and auxiliary tools (UI recorder).

By following these guidelines and tailoring the diagram with the detailed file structure and README information, your system design diagram will effectively capture the WinAppDriver project’s architecture with clearly delineated components, interactions, and important design patterns.
</explanation>
